Vegan Food in Greece

By Richard Prouse · Not yet checked on the ground · Updated 2026-11-17

Draft. This guide has not yet been checked on the ground. It is hidden from search engines until it is.

Greek Orthodox fasting has created a large tradition of food that is vegan by design, called nistisima (fasting food). Bean soups, stuffed vegetables, yellow split-pea purée and wild greens are on most taverna menus. Feta and yogurt are added by default, so ask.

How easyEasy
Word for veganvegan / νηστίσιμο (nistisimo, fasting food)
Try firstFava with onions and capers

Traditional dishes in Greece that are vegan or can be

  • Bean soup

    Fasolada

    Vegan by tradition

    White beans, tomato, celery and olive oil.

  • Yellow split-pea purée

    Fava

    Vegan by tradition

    Served with onion, capers and olive oil.

  • Baked giant beans

    Gigantes plaki

    Vegan by tradition

    Giant beans baked in tomato sauce.

  • Stuffed vine leaves

    Dolmadakia (yalantzi)

    Usually vegan: check

    The rice-only version is vegan; some contain meat.

  • Roasted vegetables

    Briam

    Usually vegan: check

    Olive-oil roasted vegetables; ask about feta.

  • Stuffed tomatoes and peppers

    Gemista

    Ask for it vegan

    Rice-filled versions are vegan; some include mince.

What to watch for in Greece

  • Feta added to salads and baked dishes
  • Yogurt in dips and sauces
  • Butter in pastries and pies
  • Minced meat in stuffed vegetables

How to ask for vegan food in Greek

Show this to your server, or print it:

Είμαι vegan. Δεν τρώω κρέας, ψάρι, αυγά, γαλακτοκομικά ή μέλι. Είναι νηστίσιμο;Eímai vegan. Den tróo kréas, psári, avgá, galaktokomiká í méli. Eínai nistísimo?

Why Greece

Greece is the number 10 most-visited country in the world, with 36.0 million international arrivals in 2024 (UN Tourism).
